verses.text: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all God's holy people in Christ Jesus at Philippi, including your leaders and servants:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God every time I think of you.
In every prayer for all of you, I pray with joy,
because you've partnered with me in sharing the Good News from the first day until now.
I'm confident that the one who began a good work in you will carry it through to completion on the day of Christ Jesus.
It's right for me to feel this way about all of you, because I hold you in my heart. Whether I'm in chains or defending and confirming the Good News, you all share in God's grace with me.
God is my witness how deeply I miss all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
Here's what I pray: that your love will keep growing in knowledge and every kind of insight,
so you can recognize what really matters and be sincere and blameless for the day of Christ,
filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to God's praise and glory.
Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that what happened to me has actually helped the Good News move forward.
My imprisonment for Christ has become clear to the whole palace guard and everyone else.
Because I'm in chains, most of the believers have become more confident in the Lord and are much bolder to speak God's word without fear.
Some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, while others do it with good intentions.
The first group preaches Christ from selfish ambition, not sincerely. They think they can make my imprisonment more painful.
The others preach from love, knowing that I'm here to defend the Good News.
So what does it matter? Either way, whether their motives are false or genuine, Christ is being announced, and that makes me glad. Yes, I'll keep rejoicing,
because I know this will lead to my deliverance through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
I eagerly hope and expect that I won't be put to shame in any way. Instead, with full courage, now as always, Christ will be honored in my body, whether I live or die.
For me, living means Christ, and dying is gain.
But if I continue to live in this body, my work will produce fruit. I'm not sure which I should choose.
I'm pulled in both directions. I want to leave this life and be with Christ, which would be far better,
but staying in this body is more necessary for your sake.
Since I'm convinced of this, I know I'll stay and continue with all of you, to help you grow and find joy in the faith,
so that when I'm with you again, you'll have even more reason to take pride in Christ Jesus because of me.

Whatever happens, live in a way worthy of Christ's Good News. Then, whether I come to see you or remain away, I'll hear that you stand firm in one spirit, working side by side with one purpose for the faith of the Good News.
Don't be frightened by your opponents in any way. Your courage is a sign of their destruction, and of your salvation—and this comes from God.
God has graciously given you the privilege not only of believing in Christ but also of suffering for him.
You're facing the same struggle you saw me have, and now hear that I still have.
